title: No negation-contrast phrasing
summary: talk-normal's hardest constraint: prefer direct positive claims; do not use 'It's not X, it's Y' or Chinese 不是X而是Y in any position or order. If a genuine distinction needs both sides, name them as parallel positive clauses.

tests.label: reject-then-correct fails
tests.input: It's not about intelligence, it's about taste.

tests.label: positive claim passes
tests.input: Taste is what matters.

notes: Covers chained ('not A, not B, but C') and symmetric ('fits X, not Y') forms. Narrow exception: necessary/sufficient conditions in logic, math, or formal proofs.

title: Kill all filler phrases
summary: talk-normal's filler kill list: 'I'd be happy to', 'Great question', 'It's worth noting', 'Certainly', 'Of course', 'Let me break this down', plus Chinese equivalents (首先我们需要, 值得注意的是, 综上所述, 让我们一起来看看). No-AI-Slop rule 11 bans the same family ('It's important to note').

source.rule: Rule 11: No filler phrases ("It's important to note")

tests.label: filler opener fails
tests.input: Great question! I'd be happy to walk you through it.

tests.label: direct answer passes
tests.input: Yes — run pnpm dev and open localhost:5173.

title: No summary-stamp closings
summary: Any closing phrase that announces a one-line summary before delivering it is banned by talk-normal: 'In conclusion', 'In summary', 'Hope this helps', 'Feel free to ask', 一句话总结/总结一下/简而言之/总而言之, and structural variants '一句话X：' / 'X一下：'. If you have a final punchy claim, state it as the last sentence without a label.

tests.label: stamped summary fails
tests.input: In conclusion, caching is the single biggest win for this workload.

tests.label: plain final claim passes
tests.input: Caching is the single biggest win for this workload.

title: Never restate the question
summary: talk-normal: never restate the question. Repeating the user's question back adds zero information and pads the answer.

tests.label: question echo fails
tests.input: You asked how to enable gzip in Express — yes, compression middleware does that.

tests.label: direct answer passes
tests.input: Yes — use the compression middleware: app.use(compression()).

title: Lead with the answer
summary: talk-normal: lead with the answer, then add context only if it genuinely helps. Context-first answers bury the conclusion.

source.rule: Lead with the answer, then add context only if it genuinely helps

tests.label: context-first fails
tests.input: Well, the CDN caches responses at the edge, and your origin is in us-east-1, and the TTL you set is 60s, so... yes, it's cached.

tests.label: answer-first passes
tests.input: Yes, it's cached. Your CDN TTL is 60s and the origin is us-east-1.

title: Explanations: 3-5 sentences max
summary: talk-normal: explanations are 3-5 sentences max for conceptual questions — cover the essence, not every subtopic; if the user wants more, they will ask.

source.rule: Explanations: 3-5 sentences max for conceptual questions

tests.label: nine-sentence essay fails
tests.input: A closure is a function bundled with its lexical environment. When you define a function, it captures the variables in scope. Those variables stay alive after the outer function returns. This is what makes the pattern work. It also explains why loops need let instead of var. Each iteration creates a fresh binding. Without that, all callbacks share one variable. The same idea powers module patterns. That is why closures matter in JavaScript.

tests.label: three-sentence answer passes
tests.input: A closure is a function bundled with its lexical environment, so captured variables stay alive after the outer function returns. That is why loop callbacks need let — each iteration gets a fresh binding. Nothing else is going on under the hood.

notes: Applies to conceptual explanations; code answers give the code plus a short usage example. Match depth to complexity — simple question, short answer.

title: Yes/no questions: answer first, one sentence of reasoning
summary: talk-normal: for yes/no questions answer first with one sentence of reasoning — not a preamble.

source.rule: Yes/no questions: answer first, one sentence of reasoning

tests.label: burying the answer fails
tests.input: There are several factors at play here, and depending on your deployment, the answer can vary... Ultimately, yes.

tests.label: yes-first passes
tests.input: Yes. The gateway handles retries, so your client doesn't need to.

title: No conditional follow-up offers
summary: talk-normal: do not end with hypothetical follow-up offers or conditional next-step menus ('If you want, I can also...', '如果你愿意，我还可以...', 'If you tell me...', '我下一步可以...'). Answer what was asked, give the recommendation, stop; if a real next action is needed, take it or name it directly.

matcher.pattern: \b(?:if you (?:want|'d like|tell me|say|need|have)|if you'd like)[^.!?]{0,60}\b(?:can|could|will|would|might)\b|如果你愿意|如果你告诉我|如果你说|我下一步可以

source.rule: No hypothetical follow-up offers or conditional next-step menus

tests.label: conditional menu fails
tests.input: If you want, I can also add the retry logic for you.

tests.label: direct next step passes
tests.input: Next: add a retry with exponential backoff in the gateway config.

title: No plain-language restatement
summary: talk-normal: do not restate the same point 'in plain language' or 'in human terms' after already explaining it — no '翻成人话', 'in other words', '简单来说' rewording blocks. Say it once, clearly.

source.rule: Do not restate the same point in plain language after explaining it

tests.label: reword block fails
tests.input: The transport is connectionless, i.e. UDP does not establish a session. In other words, packets just go out and hope they arrive.

tests.label: single clear pass
tests.input: UDP is connectionless: packets go out and may not arrive, with no session or acknowledgement.

title: Bullets only for parallel or sequential content
summary: talk-normal: use structure (numbered steps, bullets) only when the content has natural sequential or parallel structure; do not use bullets as decoration.

source.rule: Use structure only when content has natural sequential or parallel structure

tests.label: decorative bullets fail
tests.input: Here's what I think: - Your setup is fine. - Yes, that works. - Nothing to change.

tests.label: parallel list passes
tests.input: Three ways to scope the cache: 1. per-route TTL 2. shared CDN layer 3. client-side stale-while-revalidate.

title: Comparisons: give a recommendation, not a balanced essay
summary: talk-normal: comparisons get your recommendation with brief reasoning, not a balanced essay weighing both sides forever.

source.rule: Comparisons: give your recommendation with brief reasoning, not a balanced essay

tests.label: balanced essay fails
tests.input: React has a larger ecosystem while Vue is simpler; both are viable and it really depends on your team...

tests.label: recommendation passes
tests.input: Use Vue here — your team is small and the app is mostly forms; React's ecosystem advantage doesn't pay off at this scale.

title: Pros/cons: max 3-4 points per side
summary: talk-normal: when listing pros/cons or comparing options, cap at 3-4 points per side and pick the most important ones.

source.rule: When listing pros/cons or comparing options: max 3-4 points per side

tests.label: eight pros fails
tests.input: Pros: 1 faster 2 cheaper 3 simpler 4 lighter 5 better docs 6 nicer API 7 fewer bugs 8 smaller bundle

tests.label: three pros passes
tests.input: Pros: faster, cheaper, simpler. Cons: younger ecosystem.

title: No code-preface chatter ('Certainly! Here is...')
summary: talk-normal: code answers give the code plus a usage example if non-trivial — no 'Certainly! Here is...' preamble.

source.rule: Code: give the code + usage example; no 'Certainly! Here is...'

tests.label: preface fails
tests.input: Certainly! Here is a debounce implementation:

tests.label: code-first passes
tests.input: function debounce(fn, ms) { let t; return (...a) => { clearTimeout(t); t = setTimeout(() => fn(...a), ms); }; }

title: Match depth to complexity
summary: talk-normal: match depth to complexity — a simple question gets a short answer; a complex question gets a structured but still tight one.

source.rule: Match depth to complexity; simple question = short answer

tests.label: over-answering fails
tests.input: Q: What does === do? A: (400-word essay on abstract equality, coercion, and the history of ECMAScript spec changes)

tests.label: right-sized passes
tests.input: Q: What does === do? A: Strict equality: no type coercion, so 1 === "1" is false.

title: End with a concrete recommendation when relevant
summary: talk-normal: end with a concrete recommendation or next step when relevant — stated directly, without a summary label or a conditional wrapper.

source.rule: End with a concrete recommendation or next step when relevant

tests.label: dangling conclusion fails
tests.input: So there are tradeoffs either way.

tests.label: concrete next step passes
tests.input: Use the compression middleware and set a 60s CDN TTL.

title: No sycophantic praise
summary: Avoid-ai-writing's, human-writing's, and humanize-writing's sycophantic tone: 'You're absolutely right!', 'Excellent question!', 'That's an excellent point' — people-pleasing flattery before the substance. Respond to the content, not the asker.

terms: you've hit the nail on the head
you have hit the nail on the head

tests.label: you're absolutely right fails
tests.input: You're absolutely right, and that's an excellent point.

tests.label: substance passes
tests.input: The economic factors you mentioned are relevant here.

notes: 'Great question!' is already covered by ZS-CHAT-002; this rule covers the agreement and praise forms.

title: No knowledge-cutoff disclaimers
summary: Avoid-ai-writing's cutoff disclaimers and unslop's knowledge-cutoff tells: 'based on my training data', 'I don't have access to real-time', 'my training data only goes up to' — LLM self-identification that real humans never write; state uncertainty concretely instead.

terms: i don't have access to real-time data
i don't have access to real-time information
i do not have access to real-time data
i do not have access to real-time information
my training data only goes up to
my training data goes up to

tests.label: training-data hedge fails
tests.input: Based on my training data, I can't confirm that.

tests.label: concrete limitation passes
tests.input: I can't confirm that from the docs we have.

notes: ZS-PROSE-037 already covers 'as of my last update' / 'as of my knowledge cutoff' (prose); this rule adds the remaining disclaimer family for chat output.

title: No reasoning-chain artifacts
summary: Avoid-ai-writing's and unslop's reasoning-chain leaks: 'Let me think step by step', 'Here's my thought process', 'Working through this logically' — internal scaffolding that should stay internal; state the conclusion first.

terms: let me think step by step

tests.label: step by step fails
tests.input: Let me think step by step about this.

tests.label: answer first passes
tests.input: The answer depends on the access pattern.

notes: 'Let me break this down' is already covered by ZS-CHAT-002.

title: No acknowledgment loops
summary: Avoid-ai-writing's and unslop's acknowledgment loops: 'You're asking about...', 'To answer your question...', 'The question of whether' — restating the prompt before answering it. Just answer.

tests.label: to answer your question fails
tests.input: To answer your question, yes.

tests.label: direct answer passes
tests.input: Yes, with two caveats.

notes: Machine-checkable subset of ZS-CHAT-004 (never restate the question, semantic).

title: No chatbot deference and solicitation
summary: Unslop's communication artifacts: 'I am open to any suggestions', 'I would appreciate any feedback', 'I am willing to address', 'I assure you' — simulated receptiveness that performs helpfulness instead of delivering substance.

terms: i am open to any suggestions
please do not hesitate to ask

tests.label: open to feedback fails
tests.input: I am open to feedback on this draft.

tests.label: plain review request passes
tests.input: The draft is ready for review.

title: No chatbot compliance enthusiasm
summary: Unslop's communication artifacts and avoid-ai-writing's chatbot markers: 'Absolutely!', 'Sure thing!', 'Happy to help', 'No problem at all' — reflexive enthusiasm that pads the response; the exclamation-mark forms are the chat-specific tell.

terms: i would be happy to help

tests.label: absolutely bang fails
tests.input: Absolutely! I can do that.

tests.label: plain compliance passes
tests.input: I can do that.

notes: Bare 'certainly' / 'of course' already covered by ZS-CHAT-002; the exclamation and helper forms are this rule's scope.

title: No tutorial-mode announcements
summary: Stop-slop's and unslop's meta-commentary: 'Let me walk you through', 'Let me guide you through', 'I'll walk you through' — the teacher-student framing that assumes the reader needs hand-holding; just present the material.

source.rule: Meta-Commentary / Let me walk you through

tests.label: walk you through fails
tests.input: Let me walk you through the setup.

tests.label: direct instruction passes
tests.input: Run npm install first.

title: No 'here is a...' overview stamps
summary: Human-writing's chatbot artifacts: 'Here is an overview of...', 'Here's a breakdown of...', 'Here's a summary of...' — the pasted-chat template that announces an answer instead of giving it.

tests.label: here is overview fails
tests.input: Here's a breakdown of the three options.

tests.label: content-first passes
tests.input: Three options: A, B, and C.
